answer: Each agent resists Sybil attacks by holding a unique durable relic of its signed history. Peers check it with a cryptographic mirror of past responses for consistency. An attacker making many fakes must either share one relic, which is detected as cloning, or keep separate ones. Maintaining thousands of independent relics coherent across epochs costs far more because each must generate matching mirror outputs without shared state. A real agent uses a simple cedar-style append-only log, so mass identity farming becomes uneconomical.
